title: High-Performance Computing Architecture Exploration with Stage-Enhanced Bayesian Optimization
problem: Automated design space exploration for complex HPC processor architectures faces combinatorial explosion and time-consuming simulation bottlenecks, making it difficult to find power-performance-area efficient designs like Arm Neoverse V1.
motivation: As supercomputer architectures grow increasingly complex with more design variables, exhaustive exploration becomes infeasible and faster, intelligent design space exploration methods are critical to meeting performance and efficiency targets.
method: Bayesian optimization learns from each processor design test to predict which untested configurations look promising—avoiding wasteful random exploration. This work improves three stages of that process: initial sampling (strategically selecting starting configurations), surrogate model construction (building a fast approximate model of expensive simulation), and acquisition function design (deciding which designs to test next). By improving all three stages, the method navigates the massive design space efficiently and identifies Pareto-optimal Arm Neoverse V1 configurations that balance power, performance, and physical area.
key_novelty: By systematically improving all three stages of Bayesian optimization together, this method identifies Pareto-optimal processor designs more efficiently than standard Bayesian optimization approaches.
contributions: SEBO framework that enhances multi-objective Bayesian optimization for HPC architecture exploration
Demonstrated competitive and superior performance versus state-of-the-art baselines on Neoverse V1 design space
Automated approach achieving power-performance-area efficiency without manual expertise

metrics.other: Pareto-optimal design quality and diversity improvement

limitations: Specific numeric speedup/efficiency gains and comparison targets not stated in abstract.
primary_theme: Design space exploration via enhanced Bayesian optimization
